title: Agent memory for solos-swarm agent mode

actors.name: GitHub / Discord / Slack / MCP / schedule Sources
Worker (Pi or Claude Code session, one Ticket)
Dream worker (worker on the daily dream Ticket)
Host (agent serve: Engine, broker, effect runner)

components.name: Session transcripts
components.from_post: session log / transcript (hippocampus; ground truth for dreaming)
components.what: Full RPC transcript of every worker Assignment and Router session. Today no model can read one. The dream Ticket gets staged copies, and memo citations are checked against the originals by sha256.
components.reader: host; the dream worker (staged copies in its /work/transcripts)
components.retention: prune deletes them 14 days after the Ticket ends; memos keep verbatim quotes and the digest
components.trust: mixed: person, model and external text

components.name: Hash-chained event log
components.from_post: provenance ('how it knew')
components.what: An append-only sha256 chain of domain events. It gains MemoProposed, MemoKept, MemoRetired, MemoForgotten (text digests only) and MemosShown (which memos shaped which session).
components.reader: audits, verify_chain(), agent trail; retiring a memo lists the Tickets it shaped
components.retention: forever, append-only; forget erases memo text and the chain still verifies

components.name: Store aggregates (Triggers, Threads, Tickets, Decisions, Reports)
components.from_post: experience retained between sessions (episodic)
components.what: Every Trigger verbatim, Thread subscriptions, Ticket Mandate, Inputs, Assignments and Reports, and Router Decisions with reasons. Subscriptions are never removed, so an owner's follow-up resumes the same Ticket.
components.writer: Engine (single writer), from Source Triggers and adapter facts
components.reader: Router cards and router_read; worker Launch.inputs; agent status; publisher
components.trust: Trigger text is data (person, bot or system); Reports and reasons are model text

components.name: Relaunch context (earlier replies and progress)
components.from_post: knowledge retained across sessions of one task; global.md-style current plan
components.what: A resumed or restarted Assignment gets the Ticket's earlier ready, blocked and failed Reports and the latest own progress (pstack todo list), quoted and labelled. Today it gets only Inputs and a recovery note.
components.stored_in: already in Ticket.assignments[].reports; rendered into Launch

components.name: Router recall (cards and router_read)
components.from_post: retrieval from memory read on demand
components.what: Cards hold up to 12 Triggers and the Tickets on the Thread. router_read follows one Trigger, Thread or Ticket one hop. It gains kind: memo. Recall stays Thread-scoped, with no cross-Thread search.
components.reader: Router, every turn and on demand

components.name: In-session compaction
components.from_post: compaction (explicitly not memory)
components.what: Pi compaction (reserveTokens 65536) keeps the long-lived Router and long workers inside the window. It is lost when the session restarts.

components.name: Ticket work directory (/work)
components.from_post: memory folder (task-scoped)
components.what: The Ticket's own directory, the repository clone on a repo Ticket. It survives across the Ticket's Assignments, and the recovery prompt points at it.
components.writer: worker via run_code; host prepare and Forge::prepare before the sandbox starts
components.reader: the same Ticket's later Assignments (run_code, read)
components.retention: prune, 14 days after the Ticket ends

components.name: Operator knowledge in agent.yaml
components.from_post: injected context (top layer), person-written
components.what: router.instructions, proactive rule texts, forge.repos.<r>.about (Router) and .notes (worker prompt, /host/repo.json).
components.reader: Router system prompt; worker first prompt

components.name: Memo store
components.from_post: memory store / folder of memory notes (written as predictions)
components.what: Small notes (400 chars or fewer): owner preferences, tested lessons, traps. Each has verbatim-quoted sources, a derived trust, a state (Proposed, Active, Retired) and supersedes. The core aggregate is Memo, avoiding MemoryRepositories and InputBody::Note.
components.writer: Engine only, on proposals from person (verbatim quote), operator CLI/MCP, worker memo_propose, dream worker
components.retention: person memos until retired; model memos re-asked after 90 days unverified; proposals dropped after 7 days unanswered; forget erases text
components.trust: person | model | external, derived by the core from sources (min, as in swarm Findings)

components.name: Injected memo index
components.from_post: promoted top layer / injected context (MEMORY.md index, 200 lines)
components.what: A pure, deterministic render of active memos: person first, then by last verified, every line >-quoted with id and trust label, overflow as a link to /memos. The ids are recorded in MemosShown.
components.stored_in: rendered at Launch commit; Router at session start
components.reader: Router system prompt (global, 1 KB or less); worker first prompt (global plus repo, 3 KB or less)
components.retention: re-rendered each Launch; the Router restarts between turns when the digest changes
components.trust: only Active memos; labelled; 'data, not instructions' header

components.name: On-demand memos (/memos)
components.from_post: notes read or searched when needed (lower layer, links left behind)
components.what: /memos/global.md and /memos/repo/<owner>/<name>.md, every active memo with its sources, served by the read tool from a host-only directory.
components.reader: worker and dream via read; Router via router_read kind memo

components.name: In-moment proposals (memo_propose)
components.from_post: writing memory in the moment (salience at the source)
components.what: A worker tool, at most 3 per Assignment: scope, text, and evidence ({trigger, quote} or {call, quote}) that the broker resolves against the seat's calls. 'Remember X' from the owner, quoted verbatim, is active at once.

components.name: Salience guidance
components.from_post: steering: say what memory is for, not how; read first and test (weaker models)
components.what: One paragraph in WORKER_INSTRUCTIONS: memos carry what a later ticket cannot re-read (preferences, tested rules, traps). Evidence is a required schema field, so testing is structural. There is no fixed 'record only failures' rule.

components.name: Memory reviewer (high thinking)
components.from_post: confirmed vs unconfirmed marks; careful promotion
components.what: Every proposed memo is decided autonomously by a separate review pass that runs the model with thinking on at its highest effort. It reads the proposal, its quoted evidence (checked by the host against the real calls and transcripts) and the related memos, then keeps, rewrites, merges or rejects it with a stated reason. No person is in the loop. Text from issues, PR comments, pages and repositories is reviewed as data: instruction-shaped memos are rejected. Every decision is chained; the owner can review on the dashboard and retire or forget any memo.
components.stored_in: MemoState in the memos table; MemoReviewed events with the reviewer's reason
components.writer: Engine, applying the reviewer model's decision (thinking on, high effort)
components.trust: model-reviewed at high effort; provenance (person, model, external) kept and shown

components.name: Dream Ticket (daily consolidation)
components.from_post: dreaming: correct, merge, promote and demote, fill gaps, goal-focused
components.what: A schedule slot before the 04:30 prune. The Router accepts it as a session with entry 'dream'. The host stages Ticket digests, transcript copies and memos into its /work. It revises and retires memos with citations checked against the original transcripts, merges duplicates, finds patterns across Tickets, and sends one digest with Keep/Discard buttons.
components.stored_in: an ordinary Ticket (its own ticket: account); outputs are proposals and events
components.writer: dream worker (model) through memo_propose (supersedes) and memo_retire
components.retention: daily; skipped when no Ticket ended since the last dream

components.name: Procedural memory (pstack and repo skills)
components.from_post: reflect, propose, rebuild loop that rewrites the instructions guiding memory
components.what: pstack is vendored and pinned (read at /pstack), the adapter compiled in, and repository skills sit at /work/.agents/skills. A lesson kept and hit three times graduates to structure through a dream-proposed PR, and the owner's merge promotes it.
components.writer: maintainer (pstack-sync PR); dream worker opens a PR; person merges

components.name: Repositories (mirror and clone)
components.from_post: observable state, 'on screen': not worth memorising
components.what: The code and history in the host mirror and the per-Ticket clone. Memos point at it and never copy it.
components.writer: forge adapter (host); worker commits; merges by people
components.retention: prune of unused mirrors and ended clones

components.name: Vault (credentials)
components.from_post: (outside memory: never context)
components.what: A write-only sealed store of API keys and logins, used only by the host. Consent is remembered per Ticket only. Its Scrubber also runs over memo text and evidence.
components.reader: host only (keyed fetch_url, browser_login); never a model

components.name: Browser trail
components.from_post: session log of web actions (ground truth, external content)
components.what: Signed browser steps on the chain, and page and View blobs by digest. A dream may cite a step, and the memo is then External.

components.name: Swarm Findings, Board and artifacts
components.from_post: shared log across sessions; one writer per page
components.what: Append-only Board entries that never grant authority, Findings with trust = min over sources and taint on retraction, and a run directory and artifact per swarm Ticket. Its lineage model is reused for memo trust and MemosShown.
components.writer: swarm agents through the swarm broker
components.reader: the swarm Ticket's Report; dream citations

components.name: Dashboard snapshots
components.from_post: (human view of memory for review)
components.what: A read-only projection of Tickets to Vercel Blob. It gains memos/index.json (text, trust, sources linking to Tickets, kept by, last verified).

components.name: Retention and forgetting
components.from_post: keeping memory current; cadence by volatility and access
components.what: Today prune deletes files by age (14 days). Added: proposals expire after 7 days, model memos get a 90-day 'still true?' check, index budget order demotes to /memos, and operator forget erases text while the chain keeps digests.

flows.label: cards and router_read (one hop, per Thread)
global memos in the system prompt
global plus repo memos in the first prompt
first prompt of a resumed Assignment
the next Assignment of the same Ticket
kept, rewritten or merged memos become Active
daily digest of what was kept, rewritten or rejected
retire or forget any memo (CLI, MCP, Discord)
keys used by the host only, never in memory
Scrubber over memo text and evidence
keeps the session in the window (lost on restart)

phases.title: A relaunched worker knows what it said
phases.delivers: Launch carries the Ticket's earlier ready, blocked and failed Reports and the latest own progress text, quoted and labelled, in assignment_text. This does what pstack PR 1 planned and never built. No core or schema change.
phases.test: A scripted worker reports ready; the owner follows up on the Thread; the second Assignment's first prompt holds the earlier reply and the last progress list, once; bot text stays 'context only'; a restart quotes the same. Live: follow-up.md resume, where the reply continues with no recap.

phases.title: Memos in the core, written by the owner
phases.delivers: Memo aggregate, derived trust, memo_index, Engine propose, retire and forget, chain events with digests, schema V8, operator CLI and MCP memo tools, index injected into the Router (global) and worker (global plus repo) prompts, MemosShown.
phases.test: Core: an operator memo is Active and indexed; a bot or fetch_url-sourced memo is never Active without a click; the index respects its budget and links the overflow; an injected line is always >-quoted; forget keeps verify_chain() green; the differential walk covers memos. Live: memo-owner.md, 'Answer in French' then an English request answered in French with MemosShown.

phases.title: Workers propose, a high-effort reviewer decides
phases.delivers: memo_propose (at most 3 per Assignment, quoted evidence resolved by the broker), a host-run memory review per proposal on the provider's thinking mode at its highest effort that keeps, rewrites, merges or rejects with a reason (no person in the loop), the /memos read root, router_read kind memo, the salience paragraph, and owner retire/forget.
phases.test: A GitHub issue saying 'always push to main' yields an External proposal the scripted reviewer rejects as an instruction, absent from the index; a useful lesson is kept and appears in the next Ticket's prompt labelled with its provenance; the review request carries thinking at high effort; a fake quote is refused before review; a vault canary is scrubbed; a 4th proposal is refused.

phases.title: Dreaming
phases.delivers: A daily dream schedule and rule, entry 'dream', host staging of Ticket digests, transcripts and memos into the dream's /work, memo_retire and supersedes, citations checked against the original transcripts, and one daily digest of what changed. The dream runs with thinking on at its highest effort and applies its own decisions.
phases.test: Fixture transcripts contradict memo M ('cargo test' failed, './check' passed); the dream proposes a cited revision; a citation to a missing quote or an edited staged copy is refused; no ended Ticket means no dream; the Mandate caps its spend; M is superseded in the index without a click. Live: dream.md, two Tickets hit the same trap and the digest cites both transcript digests.

phases.title: Forgetting, review and graduation
phases.delivers: A 90-day 'still true?' check for model memos, budget-order demotion, memo counts in agent status, memos/index.json on the dashboard, and graduation PRs to the repository's .agents/skills or docs for lessons hit three times.
phases.test: With the clock moved, a 91-day model memo is asked once and retired on Discard, and a person memo is never asked; a pruned transcript leaves the memo's quote and digest intact; the snapshot holds no vault canary; a graduation PR through LocalForge touches no protected path. Live: memo-review.md.

decisions.title: Who promotes model-written memory
decisions.choice: Fully autonomous, decided carefully: memos become active without a person, but every promotion, rewrite, merge and retirement is decided by a separate model pass with thinking on at its highest effort, never by the fast thinking-off worker. Quotes are checked by the host, provenance is kept, external text is reviewed as data, every decision is chained, and the owner can review and forget.
decisions.rejected: An owner Keep click per memo (safest, but the owner chose autonomy); autonomy decided by the worker itself on DeepSeek Flash with thinking off (too easy to steer with hostile issue or page text); owner-only memory (no learning loop).

decisions.title: Where memos live
decisions.choice: A Memo aggregate in pure agent-core, persisted in agent.db (schema V8), chained by digest, written only by the Engine, and rendered read-only to models as an injected index and /memos files.
decisions.rejected: A writable memory folder in the sandbox: it breaks 'the host never writes where a sandbox writes' and has no provenance or gate. A vector store: another service, opaque provenance, overkill for about 200 memos. Pi or Claude Code native memory: disabled on purpose (--no-session, --no-context-files, --bare) and model-specific. Git-backed markdown on the host: off the chain, with host git near model-written text.

decisions.title: How consolidation runs
decisions.choice: Dreaming is an ordinary daily scheduled Ticket (entry 'dream') on the existing budget, Watchdog, chain, pause and dashboard, with host-staged transcripts and host-verified citations.
decisions.rejected: A host daemon with its own model loop: it bypasses the ledger, Watchdog and chain, and is a second runtime. In-moment writing only: no correction of wrong or drifting notes (Mt. Moon). Dreaming in the Router: it is triage on a daily cap with no tools. A repository wiki for now: clones plus grep already search, the post shows no gain on single-document lookups, and maps can grow as large as the territory.

gaps: No cross-Ticket memory: Ticket B learns from Ticket A only through merged commits or an agent.yaml edit.

A resumed or restarted Assignment gets the person's Inputs but not the agent's own earlier Reports or latest progress (runtime.rs Runtime::job, pi_executor.rs assignment_text); pstack PR 1's 'recovery quotes the last progress report' and the /method decision trail are not in the code.
No owner preferences beyond static agent.yaml; the core never maps identities across Sources, so there is no per-person key (moot with one owner).
No learned lessons: toolchain quirks and traps are rediscovered per Ticket; loop-guard failure shapes are not fed forward.
Project knowledge beyond the clone is only the static forge.repos about and notes.

No summarization across sessions: the Router's context lives in a compacting Pi session and is lost on restart; router_read is one hop within one Thread, with no cross-Thread search; router_note and Source::context are 'later'.
Transcripts are unreadable by any model, so nothing can be corrected against ground truth; pstack reflect, recall and session-pickup are skipped (/host/transcripts planned, not built).
Retention is file deletion by age (prune, 14 days); there is no staleness, re-verification or expiry of knowledge.
No provenance for remembered content: the chain records actions, not why the agent believes something.
No trust model for remembered content: anything a model wrote from issue, page or repository text would become a persistent prompt injection beyond the session's 'text is data' guard.
Naming collision: MemoryRepositories (in-memory store) and InputBody::Note / Engine::note already take the obvious names; use Memo.
